title: Wave 0 (W-0) — Live authority census

blocker.summary: No live database connection is reachable from a managed agent worktree. W-0 requires SQL against the deployed database; the toolkit deliberately withholds every credential that would make that possible.
evidence: web/.env.local.agent carries only public values (ALLOY_AGENT_ENV, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, feature flags). No SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, no DATABASE_URL.

scripts/local-dev/alloy-config.example:70-73 — the privileged tier (ALLOY_SERVER_ENV_SOURCE = <canonical>/web/.env.local) is injected into the toolkit-owned Next process only and is 'never copied into the worktree'.
scripts/local-dev/lib/verify.sh:293-335 — alloy_prepare_agent_env_file classifies privileged names as deny; alloy-dev-start dies if a privileged name appears in the worktree env file.
scripts/local-dev/lib/ro-capabilities.json — alloy-ro is the sanctioned read-only surface and has credential_access:false and no database verb. It inspects the toolkit, not Postgres.
No arbitrary-SQL RPC exists in supabase/migrations (no exec_sql / execute_sql / run_sql), so Q1 (pg_trigger) is unreachable through PostgREST even with a service-role key.
psql is installed (/usr/local/bin/psql); only the connection string is missing.
options_presented: A — operator runs combined_query in the Supabase SQL editor and returns the JSON row
B — operator authorizes a single read-only psql session using DATABASE_URL from the trusted env source (values never printed, never written into the worktree)
C — operator provisions a read-only Postgres role and exports its connection string for this run

target.note: The executing operator MUST record the project ref / host actually queried in execution.target_database. Wave 0's whole value is that its counts describe the database the switches will run against.

schema_grounding: public.user_roles(user_id uuid, role text, created_at, org_id uuid) — supabase/migrations/20260329165048_remote_schema.sql:2915-2920. `role` is unconstrained text (C2).
public.role_definitions(id, org_id, role_key text, role_label, description, is_system, is_active, ...) — remote_schema.sql:2701-2711
public.user_access_profiles(id, user_id, org_id, department_scope, site_scope, ...) UNIQUE(user_id, org_id) — supabase/migrations/20260504103000_user_access_scope_tables_v1.sql:18-52
public.user_profiles(id uuid, role public.app_role, ...) — remote_schema.sql:2904-2909. NOTE: no org_id column; the legacy profile role is global, and the org is recovered from app_users.

public.app_users(id uuid, role text, vendor_id, created_at, updated_at, org_id uuid NULL, auth_user_id uuid) — remote_schema.sql:1010-1019. The dual linkage (id | auth_user_id) is what the resolver walks.
resolver_grounding: web/lib/admin/resolveAdminAccessCore.ts:111-140 — the legacy fallback fires ONLY when the principal has zero user_roles rows. Q2 is therefore scoped to principals with no membership row at all.

web/lib/admin/resolveAdminAccessCore.ts:40-73 — fetchLegacyAdminOpsOrgAndRole tries user_profiles.role (org recovered from app_users by id, then auth_user_id), then app_users by id, then app_users by auth_user_id. Q2 reproduces that precedence.
web/lib/admin/resolveAdminAccessCore.ts:144-162 — absent user_access_profiles row ⇒ both scopes 'all'. Q4 counts the population that fail-open depends on.
web/lib/admin/accessScope.ts:45,51-53 — PORTAL_DEPARTMENT_SCOPE_BYPASS_ROLES = {admin, ops}. Q6 counts who is silently unrestricted today.
method.note_on_file_name: The assignment names this file wave0-authority-census.json; plan §4 originally wrote 'w0-live-census.json'. This file is authoritative and §4 has been corrected to point here.

queries.question: Is handle_new_user() attached to auth.users?
queries.sql:
SELECT t.tgname, t.tgenabled, t.tgisinternal, p.proname AS function_name
FROM pg_trigger t
JOIN pg_proc p ON p.oid = t.tgfoid
WHERE t.tgrelid = 'auth.users'::regclass
ORDER BY t.tgname;
queries.supporting_sql:
SELECT n.nspname, p.proname
FROM pg_proc p
JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace
WHERE p.proname = 'handle_new_user';
queries.reading: tgisinternal = true rows are FK/constraint triggers, not application triggers — exclude them when judging. A non-internal, enabled ('O' or 'A') trigger naming handle_new_user means G1 is LIVE: every new auth user silently receives a default role, and W-20 rises into wave 2.

queries.question: How many principals authorize ONLY via the legacy fallback (user_profiles / app_users) with no user_roles row?
queries.sql:
WITH no_membership AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id
  FROM auth.users u
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = u.id)
),
legacy AS (
  SELECT
    nm.user_id,
    (SELECT up.role::text FROM public.user_profiles up WHERE up.id = nm.user_id) AS profile_role,
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT au.org_id FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.id = nm.user_id AND au.org_id IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1),
      (SELECT au.org_id FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.auth_user_id = nm.user_id AND au.org_id IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1)
    ) AS resolved_org_id,
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT au.role FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.id = nm.user_id LIMIT 1),
      (SELECT au.role FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.auth_user_id = nm.user_id LIMIT 1)
    ) AS app_user_role
  FROM no_membership nm
)
SELECT
  count(*) AS principals_without_membership,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE profile_role IN ('admin','ops') AND resolved_org_id IS NOT NULL) AS via_user_profiles,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE app_user_role IN ('admin','ops') AND resolved_org_id IS NOT NULL) AS via_app_users,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE (profile_role IN ('admin','ops') OR app_user_role IN ('admin','ops')) AND resolved_org_id IS NOT NULL) AS legacy_only_authorized
FROM legacy;
queries.detail_sql:
-- Per-principal disposition, for the remediation list if legacy_only_authorized > 0.
WITH no_membership AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id, u.email
  FROM auth.users u
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = u.id)
)
SELECT
  nm.user_id,
  (SELECT up.role::text FROM public.user_profiles up WHERE up.id = nm.user_id) AS profile_role,
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT au.org_id FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.id = nm.user_id AND au.org_id IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1),
    (SELECT au.org_id FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.auth_user_id = nm.user_id AND au.org_id IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1)
  ) AS resolved_org_id,
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT au.role FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.id = nm.user_id LIMIT 1),
    (SELECT au.role FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.auth_user_id = nm.user_id LIMIT 1)
  ) AS app_user_role
FROM no_membership nm
ORDER BY resolved_org_id NULLS LAST;
caveats: The product uses maybeSingle() on the app_users lookups, so a principal matching MORE THAN ONE app_users row errors at runtime rather than resolving. This census uses LIMIT 1 and will count such a principal as authorized. If legacy_only_authorized > 0, check for duplicate app_users rows per principal before designing W-20's remediation.

legacy_only_authorized is the L4 lockout population: these principals lose ALL authority the moment the fallback is deleted. It is NOT the sum of via_user_profiles and via_app_users — the two overlap.

queries.question: How many user_roles.role values have no role_definitions row for that org?
queries.sql:
SELECT
  count(*) AS undefined_membership_rows,
  count(DISTINCT ur.org_id) AS orgs_affected,
  count(DISTINCT ur.role) AS distinct_undefined_roles
FROM public.user_roles ur
LEFT JOIN public.role_definitions rd
  ON rd.org_id = ur.org_id AND rd.role_key = ur.role
WHERE rd.id IS NULL;
queries.detail_sql:
SELECT ur.org_id, ur.role, count(*) AS membership_rows
FROM public.user_roles ur
LEFT JOIN public.role_definitions rd
  ON rd.org_id = ur.org_id AND rd.role_key = ur.role
WHERE rd.id IS NULL
GROUP BY ur.org_id, ur.role
ORDER BY membership_rows DESC;
caveats: The anti-join ignores role_definitions.is_active on purpose: a foreign key does not care whether the referenced row is active. Q5 reads the same join with is_active, because a grant does.
undefined_membership_rows is exactly the set that would fail M9's FK, and therefore exactly the subject of M8's remediation migration.

queries.question: How many memberships lack an access profile?
queries.sql:
WITH membership_pairs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ur.user_id, ur.org_id FROM public.user_roles ur
)
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*) FROM membership_pairs) AS distinct_user_org_pairs,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_roles) AS membership_rows,
  count(*) AS pairs_without_profile,
  count(DISTINCT mp.org_id) AS orgs_affected
FROM membership_pairs mp
LEFT JOIN public.user_access_profiles p
  ON p.user_id = mp.user_id AND p.org_id = mp.org_id
WHERE p.id IS NULL;
queries.supporting_sql:
-- The reverse direction: profile rows with no membership (orphans M1 must not touch).
SELECT count(*) AS profiles_without_membership
FROM public.user_access_profiles p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur
  WHERE ur.user_id = p.user_id AND ur.org_id = p.org_id
);
caveats: GRAIN MATTERS. user_roles is per (user, org, role) — the composite PK admits several rows per pair — while user_access_profiles is UNIQUE (user_id, org_id). M1's preflight rule 'row count == W-0 Q4' means pairs_without_profile, NOT membership_rows. Comparing against the wrong number makes the preflight pass on a wrong migration.
pairs_without_profile is the fail-open population: today each of these principals silently resolves to department_scope = all and site_scope = all.

queries.question: Does every org holding an admin/ops membership have the matching role_definitions row?
queries.sql:
WITH admin_ops_pairs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ur.org_id, ur.role
  FROM public.user_roles ur
  WHERE ur.role IN ('admin','ops')
)
SELECT
  count(*) AS admin_ops_org_role_pairs,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE rd.id IS NULL) AS pairs_with_no_definition,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE rd.id IS NOT NULL AND rd.is_active IS FALSE) AS pairs_defined_but_inactive,
  count(DISTINCT aop.org_id) FILTER (WHERE rd.id IS NULL) AS orgs_at_lockout_risk
FROM admin_ops_pairs aop
LEFT JOIN public.role_definitions rd
  ON rd.org_id = aop.org_id AND rd.role_key = aop.role;
queries.detail_sql:
WITH admin_ops_pairs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ur.org_id, ur.role
  FROM public.user_roles ur
  WHERE ur.role IN ('admin','ops')
)
SELECT aop.org_id, aop.role, (rd.id IS NOT NULL) AS definition_exists, rd.is_active
FROM admin_ops_pairs aop
LEFT JOIN public.role_definitions rd
  ON rd.org_id = aop.org_id AND rd.role_key = aop.role
WHERE rd.id IS NULL OR rd.is_active IS FALSE
ORDER BY aop.org_id, aop.role;
caveats: pairs_with_no_definition > 0 is the L2 lockout: M7 grants portal.access per role_definitions row, so an org whose memberships name admin/ops without a definition row receives no grant and loses the portal entirely at W-13 step 4.

pairs_defined_but_inactive is reported separately because an inactive definition may or may not be seeded a grant depending on M7's WHERE clause. Deciding that is W-13's job; Wave 0's job is to make sure the number is known rather than discovered.

queries.question: How many principals hold an admin/ops role AND an explicit department_scope = 'restricted' profile — i.e. are silently unrestricted today?
queries.added_by: Plan §6 W-8 states this is 'a sixth Wave 0 query in practice; add it to W-0 if W-8 is scheduled.' W-8 is in wave 2, so it is included here — it costs one more SELECT now and a second live-access authorization later.
queries.sql:
SELECT
  count(*) AS restricted_admin_ops_pairs,
  count(DISTINCT p.org_id) AS orgs_affected
FROM public.user_access_profiles p
WHERE p.department_scope = 'restricted'
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur
    WHERE ur.user_id = p.user_id
      AND ur.org_id = p.org_id
      AND ur.role IN ('admin','ops')
  );
queries.supporting_sql:
-- Same question for site scope, which is NOT bypassed today. A large gap between the two
-- numbers is evidence that operators do configure restriction and expect it to hold.
SELECT count(*) AS restricted_site_scope_pairs
FROM public.user_access_profiles p
WHERE p.site_scope = 'restricted';
caveats: restricted_admin_ops_pairs is the population whose experience CHANGES when W-8 deletes the bypass: they are configured as restricted and have never been restricted. That is a behaviour change for real operators, not a no-op, and it needs to be named before W-8 ships.

combined_query:
-- Wave 0 (W-0) live authority census — one statement, one JSON row.
-- READ-ONLY. No writes, no DDL. Safe to run in the Supabase SQL editor.
-- Paste the single returned value back into wave0-authority-census.json under "results".
WITH no_membership AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id
  FROM auth.users u
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = u.id)
),
legacy AS (
  SELECT
    nm.user_id,
    (SELECT up.role::text FROM public.user_profiles up WHERE up.id = nm.user_id) AS profile_role,
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT au.org_id FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.id = nm.user_id AND au.org_id IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1),
      (SELECT au.org_id FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.auth_user_id = nm.user_id AND au.org_id IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1)
    ) AS resolved_org_id,
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT au.role FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.id = nm.user_id LIMIT 1),
      (SELECT au.role FROM public.app_users au WHERE au.auth_user_id = nm.user_id LIMIT 1)
    ) AS app_user_role
  FROM no_membership nm
),
membership_pairs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ur.user_id, ur.org_id FROM public.user_roles ur
),
admin_ops_pairs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ur.org_id, ur.role FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.role IN ('admin','ops')
)
SELECT jsonb_pretty(jsonb_build_object(
  'census_run_at', now(),
  'database', current_database(),
  'q1_auth_users_triggers', (
    SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
      'tgname', t.tgname, 'tgenabled', t.tgenabled, 'tgisinternal', t.tgisinternal, 'function_name', p.proname
    ) ORDER BY t.tgname), '[]'::jsonb)
    FROM pg_trigger t JOIN pg_proc p ON p.oid = t.tgfoid
    WHERE t.tgrelid = 'auth.users'::regclass
  ),
  'q1_handle_new_user_defined', (
    SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace WHERE p.proname = 'handle_new_user'
  ),
  'q2_principals_without_membership', (SELECT count(*) FROM legacy),
  'q2_via_user_profiles', (SELECT count(*) FROM legacy WHERE profile_role IN ('admin','ops') AND resolved_org_id IS NOT NULL),
  'q2_via_app_users', (SELECT count(*) FROM legacy WHERE app_user_role IN ('admin','ops') AND resolved_org_id IS NOT NULL),
  'q2_legacy_only_authorized', (SELECT count(*) FROM legacy WHERE (profile_role IN ('admin','ops') OR app_user_role IN ('admin','ops')) AND resolved_org_id IS NOT NULL),
  'q3_undefined_membership_rows', (
    SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_roles ur
    LEFT JOIN public.role_definitions rd ON rd.org_id = ur.org_id AND rd.role_key = ur.role
    WHERE rd.id IS NULL
  ),
  'q3_distinct_undefined_roles', (
    SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(DISTINCT ur.role), '[]'::jsonb) FROM public.user_roles ur
    LEFT JOIN public.role_definitions rd ON rd.org_id = ur.org_id AND rd.role_key = ur.role
    WHERE rd.id IS NULL
  ),
  'q4_membership_rows', (SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_roles),
  'q4_distinct_user_org_pairs', (SELECT count(*) FROM membership_pairs),
  'q4_pairs_without_profile', (
    SELECT count(*) FROM membership_pairs mp
    LEFT JOIN public.user_access_profiles p ON p.user_id = mp.user_id AND p.org_id = mp.org_id
    WHERE p.id IS NULL
  ),
  'q4_profiles_without_membership', (
    SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_access_profiles p
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = p.user_id AND ur.org_id = p.org_id)
  ),
  'q5_admin_ops_org_role_pairs', (SELECT count(*) FROM admin_ops_pairs),
  'q5_pairs_with_no_definition', (
    SELECT count(*) FROM admin_ops_pairs aop
    LEFT JOIN public.role_definitions rd ON rd.org_id = aop.org_id AND rd.role_key = aop.role
    WHERE rd.id IS NULL
  ),
  'q5_pairs_defined_but_inactive', (
    SELECT count(*) FROM admin_ops_pairs aop
    JOIN public.role_definitions rd ON rd.org_id = aop.org_id AND rd.role_key = aop.role
    WHERE rd.is_active IS FALSE
  ),
  'q6_restricted_admin_ops_pairs', (
    SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_access_profiles p
    WHERE p.department_scope = 'restricted'
      AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = p.user_id AND ur.org_id = p.org_id AND ur.role IN ('admin','ops'))
  ),
  'q6_restricted_site_scope_pairs', (
    SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_access_profiles p WHERE p.site_scope = 'restricted'
  ),
  'org_count', (SELECT count(*) FROM public.orgs)
)) AS wave0_census;

wave_consequences.note: Filled in from results. Recorded here so the reordering rule is applied deliberately rather than remembered.

rules.condition: q1 shows a non-internal, enabled trigger running handle_new_user on auth.users
rules.consequence: G1 is promoted from latent to live; W-20 moves from wave 5 into wave 2 (plan §4).
W-20 gains a remediation step — real user_roles memberships for those principals, under §11 — scheduled explicitly ahead of the L4 switch.
M8 (remediate undefined roles) is required and its row count must equal this number before M9's FK can be applied.
M1's backfill is sized at exactly this number; W-7's fail-closed switch cannot precede it.
W-13 gains a remediation step (define the role, or correct the membership) ahead of M7, or those orgs lose the portal.
W-8 is a behaviour change for that population, not a no-op; the affected principals are named and the change is announced before the bypass is deleted.

exit_criteria.blocking_reason: counts require execution against the deployed database; see execution.blocker

consumers.consumes: Q4 — the switch is authorized only after Q4 re-runs to 0

residual_risks: Until the counts exist, every one of L1–L4 is scheduled against an unknown blast radius. Plan §4 makes citing this file a precondition for all four, so this file being count-less blocks waves 2 and 5, not merely W-0.

The queries are schema-verified against supabase/migrations in this worktree, not against the live database. If the deployed schema has drifted from migrations, a query may error rather than return a wrong number — an error is the safe failure here, but the executing operator should report it verbatim rather than adapting the SQL silently.
